name: Autonomous Quant Trading Desk
tag: A simulated trading desk where AI agents research, paper trade, check risk and write the daily close.

scenarios.title: Run one simulated trading day
scenarios.ask: Run today's session on a ${capital} paper account with a {strategy} strategy, risking {risk} per trade.
steps: Research agent
Scanned 500 sample tickers before the open and shortlisted {=6 + strategy * 2} setups that fit {strategy}.
Trader agent
Placed {=4 + strategy} simulated orders, each sized so a stop-out loses no more than ${=round(capital * risk / 100)}.
Risk agent
Checked exposure every 15 minutes against a daily loss limit of ${=round(capital * risk * 3 / 100)}.
Close writer
Wrote the end-of-day summary: fills, open positions, rule breaks and notes for tomorrow.
followups: Does it ever place real orders?
No. This desk runs on simulated fills only. It is built for testing ideas and process, not for live trading.
Why size trades by risk instead of dollars?
Sizing by risk means every trade can lose about the same amount, ${=round(capital * risk / 100)} here, no matter how far away the stop is. That keeps one bad trade from dominating the day.

scenarios.title: Test a risk limit breach
scenarios.ask: We hold {positions} paper positions. What happens if the account falls {drop} in one day?
steps: Scenario builder
Applied a {drop} drop across all {positions} positions using sample prices.
Risk agent
Compared the loss with the {limit} daily limit.
Trader agent
Under the rules, closes the weakest {=ceil(positions * 0.4)} positions first if the limit is crossed.
Close writer
Logged the event with times, prices and which rule fired.
followups: Yes. Limits, which positions close first and cool-down periods are plain settings. Each change is logged so you can compare runs.
Does the desk stop for the day after a breach?
By default it stops opening new trades for the rest of the session and flags the breach in the close summary.

scenarios.title: Review a week of simulated trading
scenarios.ask: Summarize the last {days} sessions across {agents} agent schedules.
steps: Scheduler
Confirmed {=days * agents} scheduled agent runs. {=max(0, round(days * agents * 0.03))} ran late.
Analyst
Grouped {=days * 6} paper trades by setup type and time of day.
Risk agent
Counted rule breaks and near misses for each session.
Close writer
Wrote a one-page weekly review with what to keep, cut or test next.
followups: Can I see why the agent took a trade?
Yes. Every simulated trade keeps the research note, the rule that triggered it and the risk check that approved it.
It helps test process and rules. It does not predict future results, and simulated fills can be kinder than real markets.
